title: An award that rewrote the deal

scenes.dialogue: Hi, I am Ravishankar from LawWorld. Can arbitrators order specific performance at six times the agreed rate, on terms the contract never contained?
On twenty ninth October, a two-judge Supreme Court bench of Honourable Justice Sanjay Kumar and Honourable Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva ruled.
scenes.shown: On 29 October, a two-judge Supreme Court bench of Honourable Justice Sanjay Kumar and Honourable Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva ruled.

scenes.dialogue: In two thousand three, landowners gave a builder the right to develop their two ninth share at Panchpakhadi, Thane, at nine hundred fifteen rupees per square foot of F S I.
scenes.shown: In 2003, landowners gave a builder the right to develop their 2/9th share at Panchpakhadi, Thane, at ₹915 per square foot of FSI.

scenes.dialogue: Time was of the essence; conveyance would follow only full payment. The balance was not fully paid by first March two thousand eight, and the owners terminated the agreement.
scenes.shown: Time was of the essence; conveyance would follow only full payment. The balance was not fully paid by 1 March 2008, and the owners terminated the agreement.

scenes.dialogue: In twenty eleven, the majority award called the termination illegal, and granted the builder specific performance at six times the agreed rate.
scenes.shown: In 2011, the majority award called the termination illegal, and granted the builder specific performance at six times the agreed rate.

scenes.dialogue: It also took in part of the excluded property, and fixed alternative damages. The District Judge upheld the award, but the Bombay High Court set it aside.
Testing the award under the unamended Section Thirty Four, the Supreme Court held that rewriting the contract violates Section Twenty Eight, sub section Three.
scenes.shown: Testing the award under the unamended Section 34, the Supreme Court held that rewriting the contract violates Section 28(3).

scenes.dialogue: Development deal or sale, the label did not matter; the terms did. And, the Court said, the two arbitrators supplanted them with new terms, as per their own fancies.
scenes.shown: Development deal or sale, the label did not matter; the terms did. And, the Court said, the two arbitrators supplanted them with new terms, "as per their own fancies."

scenes.dialogue: The award could not be upheld. But the owners kept the money, so under Article One Forty Two, they must refund it with nine percent simple interest a year.
scenes.shown: The award could not be upheld. But the owners kept the money, so under Article 142, they must refund it with 9% simple interest a year.
